text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Human Rt said it was requesting the requalification of its shares to the "listed A" category of the Budapest Stock Exchange from the "listed B" where they are traded now.
"I think we should belong to this elite group," Human's Finance Director Gyula Rudolf told Reuters. "Our request is underway."
Rudolf said investors raised the issue of requalifacation at Human's annual general meeting earlier this year and company officials promised to review the issue at the end of 1996.

Human, majority-owned by Canada's Novopharm Ltd already meets one of the most important conditions set for companies in the "listed A" category, namely that it quarterly releases its figures although it would have to do so only every half year.
Differences between the "listed A" and "listed B" categories of the Hungarian bourse include stricter obligations on providing information.
On the Budapest bourse Human shares stood at 2,590 forints, down 50 from Tuesday's close, at 1223 GMT.
